prompt:
You are a formal verification assistant. The following Dafny program fails Dafny verification.

=== PROGRAM ===
method CopyMatrix(src: array2, dst: array2)
    requires src.Length0 == dst.Length0 && src.Length1 == dst.Length1
    modifies dst
    ensures forall i, j :: 0 <= i < src.Length0 && 0 <= j < src.Length1 ==> dst[i,j] == old(src[i,j]) 
{
    var m := 0;
    while m != src.Length0
        invariant 0 <= m <= src.Length0
        invariant forall i, j :: 0 <= i < m && 0 <= j < src.Length1 ==> dst[i,j] == old(src[i,j]) 
        invariant forall i, j :: 0 <= i < src.Length0 && 0 <= j < src.Length1 ==> src[i,j] == old(src[i,j])
    {
        var n := 0;
        while n != src.Length1
            invariant 0 <= n <= src.Length1 
            invariant forall i, j :: 0 <= i < src.Length0 && 0 <= j < src.Length1 ==> src[i,j] == old(src[i,j])
            invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < n ==> dst[m,j] == old(src[m,j])
        {
            dst[m,n] := src[m,n]; n := n + 1;
        }
        m := m + 1; 
    }
}

=== DAFNY ERROR ===
program.dfy(9,18): Error: this invariant could not be proved to be maintained by the loop
 Related message: loop invariant violation

Dafny program verifier finished with 1 verified, 1 error

=== COUNTEREXAMPLE ===
At initial state: dst.Length0 = 9600, dst.Length1 = 2261, src.Length0 = 9600, src.Length1 = 2261. At a program state: m = 0.

Analyze the failure and respond with ONLY a valid JSON object — no explanation, no markdown, no code fences. Use exactly this structure:

{
  "spec_element": "<one of: requires | invariant | ensures>",
  "proof_obligation": "<one of: initiation | preservation | bridge>",
  "diagnosis": "<explanation of what broke and why>",
  "repair": "<the corrected Dafny specification line that restores the intended behavior>"
}

Definitions:
- requires: the precondition that must hold before the method executes
- invariant: the loop invariant that must hold throughout the loop
- ensures: the postcondition that the method must guarantee on return
- initiation: the precondition does not establish the invariant at loop entry
- preservation: the loop body does not maintain the invariant
- bridge: the invariant and loop exit condition do not imply the postcondition
raw_response: {"spec_element": "invariant", "proof_obligation": "preservation", "diagnosis": "The outer-loop invariant on line 9 says rows 0..m-1 of dst already equal old(src). After the inner loop and m := m + 1, the verifier therefore cannot prove that rows 0..m-1 still hold old(src) values. The counterexample (m = 0 going to m = 1) reflects this lost frame information. The fix is to carry the completed-rows fact through the inner loop as an extra inner invariant. The inner loop only writes row m, so this invariant is preserved. Together with the row-m invariant at n == src.Length1, it re-establishes line 9 for m + 1.", "repair": "invariant forall i, j :: 0 <= i < m && 0 <= j < src.Length1 ==> dst[i,j] == old(src[i,j])"}

There's also a subtler issue: if src and dst alias, writing dst[m,n] from src[m,n] should be a no-op, but I need to check whether that assumption actually holds under the stated invariants.
